'''Lars-Erik Tammelin''' (16 March 1923 – 3 January 1991) was a Swedish [[chemist]], defence researcher and civil servant. Tammelin served as Director-General of the [[Swedish National Defence Research Institute]] from 1984 to 1985.

==Early life==
Tammelin was born on 16 March 1923 in [[Stockholm]], Sweden, the son of Supreme Court Justice {{ill|Erik Tammelin|sv}} and his wife Elsa (née Palm).<ref name="Burling (1962), p. 1058">{{cite book |editor1-last=Burling |editor1-first=Ingeborg |date=1962 |title=Vem är det: svensk biografisk handbok. 1963 |trans-title=Who is it: Swedish biographical handbook. 1963 |location=Stockholm |publisher=Norstedt |language=sv |url=https://runeberg.org/vemardet/1963/1074.html  |id={{LIBRIS|9649168}} |page=1058}}</ref>

==Career==
Tammelin, who was an [[Organic chemistry|organic chemist]], was recruited to the [[Swedish National Defence Research Institute]] (FOA) in 1950 for research on [[nerve gas]] and nerve gas [[countermeasure]]s. At this time, FOA (whose previous [[chemical warfare]] activities had focussed on [[mustard gas]] and other [[World War I]]-style compounds) had become aware that large quantities of nerve gas, primarily [[Tabun (nerve agent)|Tabun]], had been stockpiled during World War II.<ref>{{cite book |editor-last1=Littke |editor-first1=Ann Kathrine |editor-last2=Sundström |editor-first2=Olle |title=Försvarets forskningsanstalt 1945–1995 |chapter=Nervgasforskning under två decennier – en översikt |trans-chapter=Nerve gas research during two decades – an overview |first=Lennart |last=Larsson |year=1995 |publisher=Probus |location=Stockholm |language=sv |isbn=91-87184-39-7 |id={{LIBRIS|7762924}} |pages=185–188}}</ref> The mechanism of action of the nerve gases were found to be linked to their chemical similarity to the [[neurotransmitter]] [[acetylcholine]] and their ability to block the [[enzyme]] [[cholinesterase]]. Much of Tammelin's work was therefore focussed on choline [[ester]]s. In 1958, he defended a PhD thesis based on this work at [[Stockholm University|Stockholm University College]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Tammelin |first=Lars-Erik |title=Choline esters: substrate and inhibitors of cholinesterases |year=1958 |location=Stockholm |id={{LIBRIS|9470776}}}}</ref> The same year he became [[Docent]] in organic chemistry at Stockholm University College.<ref name="Vem är det (1984), p. 1090">{{cite book |date=1984 |title=Vem är det: svensk biografisk handbok. 1985 |trans-title=Who is it: Swedish biographical handbook. 1985 |location=Stockholm |publisher=Norstedt |language=sv |isbn=91-1-843222-0 |url=https://runeberg.org/vemardet/1985/1090.html |id={{LIBRIS|3681527}} |page=1090}}</ref>

The esters that form analogues to the [[Nerve agent#V-series|V-Series of nerve agents]] are sometimes referred to as "Tammelin's esters".  [[Succinylcholine]], one of the compounds synthesized by Tammelin in his search for nerve gas countermeasures, was put into use as a [[muscle relaxant]] for use during [[general anaesthesia]] surgery under the brand name Celocurin.

In 1961, Tammelin became head of the chemical-medical division at FOA, when he succeeded [[Gustaf Ljunggren (chemist)|Gustaf Ljunggren]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Agrell |first=Wilhelm |author-link=Wilhelm Agrell |title=Svenska förintelsevapen: utvecklingen av kemiska och nukleära stridsmedel 1928–1970 |year=2002 |publisher=Historiska media |location=Lund |language=sv |isbn=91-89442-49-0 |id={{LIBRIS|8415678}} |page=200}}</ref> Tammelin became a medical honorary doctorate at [[Karolinska Institutet]] in 1973.<ref name="Vem är det (1984), p. 1090"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://ki.se/sites/default/files/hedersdoktorer_130522.pdf |publisher=[[Karolinska Institutet]] |title=Karolinska Institutet Medicine hedersdoktorer 1910–2013 |trans-title=Karolinska Institutet honorary doctors of medicine 1910–2013 |access-date=4 April 2016 |language=sv |archive-date=1 May 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150501122820/http://ki.se/sites/default/files/hedersdoktorer_130522.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was professor and research director of the [[National Food Administration (Sweden)|National Food Administration]] from 1975 to 1982<ref name="Vem är det (1984), p. 1090"/> and Director-General of FOA from 1984 to 1985.

==Personal life==
In 1946 he married Isa Nilson (born 1922), the daughter of factory manager Nils Konrad Nilson and Sigrid Johansson.<ref name="Burling (1962), p. 1058"/>

==Death==
Tammelin died on 3 January 1991 and was buried at [[Bromma Church|Bromma Cemetery]] on 10 April 1991.<ref name="Uddling & Paabo (1992), p. 1271">{{cite book |editor1-last=Uddling |editor1-first=Hans |editor2-last=Paabo |editor2-first=Katrin |date=1992 |title=Vem är det: svensk biografisk handbok. 1993 |trans-title=Who is it: Swedish biographical handbook. 1993 |location=Stockholm |publisher=Norstedt |isbn=91-1-914072-X |language=sv |url=https://runeberg.org/vemardet/1993/1271.html |id={{LIBRIS|8261513}} |page=1271}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://svenskagravar.se/gravsatt/680b73e9-60d3-476a-81ec-c4d336f8c1dc |website=svenskagravar.se |title=Tammelin, Lars-Erik |access-date=11 December 2023 |language=sv}}</ref>
